speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
What you think of the effort? Delighted with the effort,  
thought it was terrific. Losing a  goal so early in any game’s tough,  
but especially against a team with the quality of  Celtic. Kind of feared the worst—I think it was  
50 seconds or something. But they dug in, they  battled manfully to get us back in the game,  
caused them a couple of problems first half  with the ball, not as much in the second  
half that they’d like. But the actual sort of  work rate, desire, shape, whatever it was, um,  
without the ball, I thought it was really,  really good—something for us to build on.
Show character today after this? Yeah, listen, the players at the  
end of the day—I’m not saying this selfishly, I’m  not—but they just need to look after themselves.  
They’re a really good group, they’re an honest  bunch of lads, they’re great to work with,  
but I think they did show the character. You  know, they scored the third late on without  
really putting them under any pressure to try  and get the equalizer. It’s still a late third  
goal that ultimately sort of—there’s no way  coming back from that. But no, I’m really  
pleased with the character and, as I say, it’s a  starting point for us to try and kick on again.
Is that a return to form? Well, I think we can play  
better. I think—and it’s something that myself  and the manager were constantly hammering them  
about—was to be better with the ball. We’ve got  good players, maybe sometimes a lack of belief,  
maybe trust in themselves, trust in their  teammates. But we need to be better at it in  
big moments of the game. If you’re defending  like that for so long and you win it back,  
you need to be good with the ball and try  and cause them problems at the other end.  
And it’s something that we need to strive to  continue to work on and hopefully get better at.
Obika strong with the real hand? Yeah, his work rate was phenomenal.  
You know, he’s a bustling, probably old-fashioned  striker, and to give that level of performance,  
work rate—there’s a couple of times we were  thinking we need to take him off, and he just  
kept going. And as I say, I think that was—I  think that was sort of showing throughout the  
team. One or two with knocks and bumps in there,  but even Dominic Thompson—he was cramping up,  
I was ready to take him off, and he said,  ‘No, leave me.’ He went for about another 15,  
20 minutes or so. That’s the attitude  we need, and that will be the attitude  
that will take us forward and keep  them hopefully going up the league.
You spoke about getting that connection back  between the fans and the players before the  
game—do you feel like you had that today? I hope so. I felt it. As I said, at halftime,  
we were 2-1 down, really, really disappointed.  But there was an energy in the dressing room.  
The players felt it, and they felt that they  were getting a lot of energy from the fans.  
What’s happened this week has happened, and I  did say it during the week—it feels as though  
the whole fanbase has been tested by this. But  it’s done, it’s dusted. And I think, hopefully,  
we did give some sort of connection  back. That’s down to the players,  
but it’s also down to the fans appreciating the  effort they saw on the pitch this afternoon.
Have you been given a timeframe for  
what happens next in terms of the job? No. David just tasked me with the game.  
Honestly, just with the game this afternoon.  We’re gutted there’s no game next weekend in the  
Scottish Cup, but it might give the club a bit of  time to take a breather, to get everything settled  
down, hopefully get the right person in place that  can take this fantastic football club forward.  
We’ve got great people at it, and hopefully,  we can keep going in the right direction.
What did you feel Will and Luke will be  able to add to the group going forward? 
We didn’t get enough to show Luke Plange with  his style of play because of that lack of quality  
possibly in the second half. So he will add  quality up front, he’ll get goals, he’s got pace,  
and he can link the game. Will’s more of a ball  carrier, but there was one time where he was  
playing like a number eight in the middle of the  pitch. Then off the chain, he goes as a number  
10. Never phased him. And there were a couple  of times you see him, and you think, ‘Well,  
he can look after the ball.’ So I think he’ll add  that to it. It’s another couple in the group, and  
hopefully, they can push the ones we’ve got here  to go and have a successful end of the season.
Are you happy to continue in this role? I’ve got a call later on this evening with  
the head of recruitment, so we’ll have a wee  chat, see what’s going on. But I’m happy to do  
whatever the club needs. As I say, it’s far  from a burden coming in here every morning.  
It’s a pleasure to come in every morning, work  with the people, the staff that I work with—not  
just the coaching side, everyone in the offices.  It’s a small club with a real family ethos  
and a group of players who, since Tuesday,  haven’t had to pick themselves up. They’ve  
been terrific. So until I’m told otherwise,  I’ll continue to give all I can for the club.
Are you anticipating movement  the other way tomorrow as well? 
There’s always a chance, yeah. There’s  always a chance of that. There’s one or  
two who obviously didn’t make the bench today.  The squad’s increased a little bit with the new  
signings over the last week or so, so that’s a  conversation I’ll have this afternoon with Nick.
title: Stephen Frail Full Post Match Press Conference | Motherwell 3-1 Celtic
